transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2029-02-07 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 54 minutes
- Attendees: Priya Shah (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Marta Lopez (Nectar - Head of Search), Eli Zhang (Nectar - ML Eng), Jordan Patel (Nectar - Infra)

Auto-Summary (auto-generated): Discussed hosting options (hosted/dedicated/private), vector DB choices and integration patterns, embedding dim tradeoffs (768 vs 1536), hybrid rerank approaches, throughput and tail latency targets, next steps to run a benchmark.

Topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; Vector DB integration (Pinecone / self-hosted Milvus); Reranking budget and where to run it; KV/prefix cache; quantization and dimension reduction options.

Transcript:
[00:00] Priya (Redwood): hey all, thanks for joining, um this is Priya from Redwood, with Daniel our solutions engineer. my plan is quick intro then dive into your current stack and throughput targets.
[00:20] Marta (Nectar): hi, thanks. we run customer search and recommendations, currently embeddings in Pinecone, rerank as a small service that calls OpenAI embeddings for new content then runs a light transformer rerank on CPU. thinking about moving embedding compute to be closer to inference to reduce tail lat.
[00:40] Daniel (Redwood SE): got it. when you say tail lat, what's your p95 target?
[00:46] Marta: right now p95 is about 250ms for the search path end-to-end; we want to get p95 under 120ms if possible for our premium tier.
[00:55] Eli (Nectar): and peak QPS is spiky—weekend flash sales we see bursts to ~600 qps sustained for a few minutes, baseline 80-120 qps.
[01:10] Jordan (Nectar): infra constraint: everything needs to keep in our VPC for PCI/regulatory reasons — so private or VPC-hosted is preferred, but we also want a managed offering if possible.
[01:25] Priya: great, we usually discuss three options: Hosted (fastest onboarding), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools + predictable throughput), and Private (VPC or on-prem for compliance). for your VPC constraint, Redwood Private can run with a customer-managed control plane.
[01:45] Marta: can you explain where rerank would live? currently it's a separate microservice — do you recommend we do rerank inside Redwood or keep it in our infra?
[01:55] Daniel: two patterns we see: 1) embedding + nearest-neighbor in a vector DB, then send top N to a rerank model — that rerank can be hosted in Redwood runtime so the rerank latency is lower because it's collocated with the model and cache; or 2) keep rerank inside customer infra and call Redwood only for embeddings, this reduces data movement but can add network tail latency. both are valid depending on compliance.
[02:30] Marta: what about cost? reranking every query sounds expensive.
[02:34] Priya: yeah, so hybrid approaches work well: do a cheap lexical+embedding hybrid prefilter then rerank only top 10 or 20. Redwood also has intelligent batching and KV/prefix caching to amortize cost. we can show numbers on cost per 100k queries in the follow-up.
[02:55] Eli: when you say KV cache, do you mean model kv cache or caching of embedding lookups?
[03:01] Daniel: both. the runtime has a KV cache for autoregressive models' key/value states to speed up generation, and we support prefix caching and embedding cache for repeated queries. in vector DB integration we typically cache top-k responses for very hot queries to avoid repeated NN lookups.
[03:20] Jordan: we use Milvus in a dev cluster and pinecone in prod; are there recommended sharding patterns?
[03:27] Daniel: sharding depends on devs. for 600 qps spikes you can either scale vector DB horizontally or use a hybrid fallback where a cheaper lower-dim embedding is used for fanout then a higher-precision rerank. another pattern is sharded nearest-neighbor with replicate routing for hot partitions.
[03:49] Marta: dims question — we currently use 1536 dims from OpenAI; is it worth dropping to 768 or quantizing?
[03:57] Priya: tradeoffs: 1536 gives better semantic fidelity but higher storage and retrieval cost. 768 or quantized embeddings drastically reduce I/O and speed up vector DB queries. We often recommend running a small eval (A/B) to measure recall impact; Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles per workload.
[04:20] Eli: our rerank model is a small transformer that takes top 50 candidates — latency becomes the killer. any suggestions?
[04:27] Daniel: if rerank is the bottleneck, options: 1) reduce candidate set to top 10 with a stronger hybrid prefilter, 2) run rerank on dedicated GPUs (Redwood Dedicated) for steady low-latency, or 3) run quantized rerank models with smaller int8 kernels. we can help bench those.
[04:50] Marta: what about vector DB vendor lock? we don't want to be tied — is Redwood flexible?
[04:55] Priya: yes, we integrate with multiple vector DBs and provide abstraction. we support streaming writes to Pinecone/Milvus/Weaviate and can run local ANN indexes as a fallback.
[05:10] Jordan: security questions — SSO, audit logs, KMS — what do you provide?
[05:16] Priya: Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM integration, full audit logs, SOC2-level controls; we can share our security pack. for Hosted we offer encryption at rest, role-based access, and enterprise SSO. we'll attach the security deck.
[05:30] Marta: any real customer examples of similar workloads?
[05:34] Daniel: yes, a retail customer had similar spikes and used dedicated pools + hybrid rerank, shaved p95 from 300ms to ~90ms with quantization and a top-10 rerank.
[05:50] Eli: what's the expected bench plan? we need to simulate our query distribution and doc corpus.
[05:55] Daniel: plan would be: you provide sample corpus (~500k docs) and query trace; Redwood runs two passes: hosted baseline and dedicated/private config; measure throughput, p50/p95/p99, cost per qps. we'll use Locust/JMeter and our inference harness.
[06:20] Marta: timeline — how long to run bench?
[06:23] Daniel: small smoke tests in 1-2 days, full runs a week depending on queue.
[06:30] Jordan: do you support on-prem? because our compliance might require air-gapped.
[06:34] Priya: yes, Private can be on-prem packaged; there are more lead-time and ops responsibilities but doable.
[06:45] Marta: ok, next steps?
[06:48] Priya: I'll send pricing and a hosting comparison, Daniel will draft the benchmark plan and test harness, Eli will upload a sample corpus and query mix. then we schedule a kickoff for the POC.
[07:00] (crosstalk) Eli: yeah I'll try to get the anonymized traces by Friday.
[07:05] Priya: perfect. any other concerns?
[07:08] Marta: just one — how do you handle model rollouts and regressions in rerank quality? we need eval hooks.
[07:15] Daniel: Redwood has eval and quality monitoring tied to prompt sets and eval suites; you can pin model versions and we can run automated regression tests on new model rollouts.
[07:30] Marta: great. thanks everyone.
[07:33] Priya: thanks, we'll follow up with the doc pack and the benchmark plan.
[07:37] Jordan: thanks all.

Meeting ended 15:54 UTC.
